source_boundaries.finding: _determine_batch_execution_and_padding initializes should_ubatch=False; no local branch enables it; allow_microbatching does not enable a two-work path
GDN _build_attn_group_metadata rejects any non-None ubid, not merely the second stream
One runner-owned unpadded gdn_query_start_loc buffer; dummy/capture path explicitly disables ubatch slices
Public worker boundary initializes one workspace owner and delegates an entire scheduler step to model_runner.execute_model; it does not expose a GDN/MoE stage continuation

Forward metadata is a scoped module-global context; two unsynchronized Python threads cannot independently own it. Sequential host submission under restored contexts may be possible only with separately valid metadata and lifetimes, not demonstrated here.

GDN obtains metadata by prefix from the current context, uses layer-owned kv_cache, and writes conv/recurrent states by metadata state indices. Different token slices may still write the same request state.

Routing owns sorted_hidden_states, expanded_row_idx, expert_tokens/group_list and combine metadata per invocation. Independent GMM input must preserve these actual per-microbatch outputs, not fabricate counts from a dimension of 256.
Typed MoE MLP boundary accepts already dispatched inputs and returns after GMM2; it is not an executor interface for creating or resuming the other microbatch's GDN.

public_interface_assessment.worker_cls: A custom worker is public and could host a new executor, so universal impossibility is NOT claimed. Implementing a replacement hybrid metadata builder and staged runner, or copying whole forwards, is not a stream/event-only adapter to the current supported path. public_interface_assessment.safe_stop: Do not delete assertions, replace global forward context concurrently, copy/patch host forward methods, restore cascade, or present unrelated random kernels as production overlap. Stop this current-host scheduling-only path at the reproduced interface gate.
